text:
maria: follow-up thread for the authn/authz migration spike. focusing on shadow-issuance, audit continuity, and low-friction rollouts. link to notes: https://rfc/redwood/authn-migration

devin: nice. i'd like to clarify shadow-issuance mode. do we mint new identity-keys but not rotate client creds immediately?

maria: exactly. shadow-issuance means we create identity-keys mapped to canonical_principal and issue session tokens in parallel while leaving legacy keys accepted. no client-side change required until opt-in rotation

sam: operationally, how does billing/metrics handle dual issuance? we shouldn't double-count traffic during shadow period

ben: plan: use canonical_id as the billing anchor. both legacy and shadowed identity map to the same canonical_id; telemetry pipeline dedups by canonical_id and request id

zoe: addendum: ensure logs include issuer_type (legacy|shadow|rotated) so we can track adoption rate. small change to our logging schema

lina: revocation story? if a legacy key is revoked we should break both legacy and shadow flows immediately

maria: revoke by canonical_id: revocation service emits events tagged with canonical_id and any active session_ids. runtime subscribes and evicts caches. legacy acceptance checks canonical revoke state on auth path

devin: latency concern: revocation event to edge could be >500ms in some zones. we should document eventual consistency for revocation until 2s window

sam: also need a fast-path for emergency immediate block: short-circuit at gateway to reject based on a small in-memory blacklist for high-risk keys

ben: migration CLI: two modes: preview (scan + report mapping) and execute (create identity-keys + optional rotate). Will emit plan.json that operators can review

zoe: for execute mode, include dry-run flag and validation checks: service ownership verification, KMS availability, and webhook callbacks to notify client teams

maria: good. also add shadow-issuance TTL default 90 days. after TTL we can auto-rotate or force deprecation depending on policy

lina: how to handle integrators that rely on org-wide/global roles? delegation tokens only or special org-identity?

devin: prefer delegation objects minted by the org owner. we might allow org-level identity-keys for internal monoliths but mark them high-risk and require stricter audits

sam: RBAC mapping: during migration we must preserve effective permissions. algorithm: canonical_principal inherits existing role grants; new identity-key gets same grants. session token permissions = intersection(requested_scopes, identity_grants)

ben: auditing: every mint/exchange must write an immutable audit record with fields [canonical_id, issuer_type, session_id, requested_scopes, outcome, actor_ip]. we'll forward these to long-term audit store

zoe: storage note: audit store should be append-only with retention policy per org; add a quick index by session_id for lookup on incident response

maria: docs: add migration playbook with checklist: backup auth DB, enable shadow-issuance, run preview scan, schedule rotate waves, monitor metrics, close window. target small batches first

lina: monitoring: add a dashboard for adoption rate (pct traffic using rotated credentials), revocation latency histogram, and auth error spikes by canonical_id

devin: testing: create e2e harness that simulates 5k legacy keys, runs shadow-issuance, performs revocation spike, and measures 95p latency for token exchange and auth path

sam: security review: ensure identity-keys created by migration cli are created with least-permission and never printed in CI logs. require "rotate-once" secret output only to KMS

ben: enterprise/private customers: tool will optionally create HSM-protected identity-keys and provide guidance for on-prem KMS plugins

zoe: question: timeline and deprecation header behavior. we should start sending Deprecation header immediately when compatibility shim is enabled for a tenant

maria: agreed. Deprecation header + Retry-After-esque Advisory header with migration window and docs link. we'll default to 180 days for public tenants

infra-bot: CI: "auth-migration-cli" PR opened. unit tests pass, security scans in progress. e2e migration suite queued on staging

lina: i'll take revocation latency spike tests. Devin can pair on harness setup

devin: on it. scheduling a 45min pairing tomorrow 10am PT

maria: i'll prepare the rollout checklist and publish a calendar invite for stakeholders. thanks everyone

sam: :+1:
